mappings.note: Completes the Vedic line about noble thoughts coming from all directions, cited as an inherited value behind the Constitution's openness. Constitutional values under the goal.
Inviting public comment on draft laws read as citizen participation in democracy. The working of democratic process, so the goal.
The keyed value is justice and the protection of individual liberty, not equality alone, so the goal rather than LO-198 even though equal treatment appears in the stem.
Matches the original illustrations to the Parts they head, with one wrong pairing. A fact about the document under the goal.

Junior students' voices being drowned out is a failure of equal representation (LO-198), while part (ii) asks what a constitution or rulebook is for and part (iii) asks for a fair procedure (CG-SST3).
A ban on a peaceful religious practice tested in court engages liberty of belief, the secular character of the state and the judiciary's role. Liberty rather than equality, so the goal.
Villagers invoke a Fundamental Right and a Directive Principle (CG-SST3), and the harm they complain of is untreated factory effluent poisoning their water, which is the pollution outcome (LO-191).
What liberty guarantees in the Preamble. A Preamble value with no outcome of its own, so the goal.
Explains the Preamble's ideal of equality. The equality outcome stated directly.
What fraternity promotes among citizens. A Preamble value under the goal; LO-198 is kept for equality.
How the freedom struggle answered practical questions about structuring government. The making of the Constitution, so the goal.
What the historical and cultural illustrations in the original signify. Constitutional values under the goal.
The qualities Rajendra Prasad said democratic institutions need. Constitutional values and civic conduct under the goal.
How the Constitution balances Central and State powers. Not LO-201, whose wording is about local versus State government; this item is about the Centre and the States.
Why a diverse country needs a constitution, argued through the kabaddi-rules analogy. The purpose of a constitution under the goal.
Evaluates the Assembly's composition and why breadth of representation mattered. The making of the Constitution under the goal.
Why a country needs a constitution at all. The goal's own subject.
The rulebook analogy for the Constitution. The purpose of a constitution under the goal.
How the Constituent Assembly was formed. The drafting process under the goal.
The Drafting Committee's role under Ambedkar. The drafting process under the goal.
How the freedom struggle shaped the Constitution's values. Sources of constitutional values under the goal.
An example of civilisational heritage influencing the Constitution. Sources of constitutional values under the goal.
Checks and balances among the organs of government. A constitutional principle under the goal.
The difference between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles. Constitutional structure under the goal.
